contracts.title: Source copyright and notice boundary
sourceCharacterization: Root LICENSE declares MIT and Copyright (c) 2026 Lovecast Inc.; preserve the permission and copyright notice in reused source/substantial portions.
This is repository-level source provenance, not evidence that every embedded brand, recording, portrait or sound was authored by the licensor or separately authorized.
No external rights verification was performed. Unknown origin means unknown, not an infringement finding or permission to redistribute.
futureAcceptance: Bind each reused binary/vector/dependency to a versioned origin and applicable notice or obtain root-approved independent replacement; verify notices in the distributable.

contracts.title: Bundled font and dependency-art notices
sourceCharacterization: Renderer CSS loads Geist variable 100–900 with swap and Symbols Nerd Font Mono 400 restricted to private-use unicode; KaTeX CSS imports its dependency font assets.

Nerd Font has adjacent OFL 1.1 notice naming Ryan L McIntyre (2014). Geist has an OFL 1.1 notice under docs/site naming Vercel (2023), collaboration with basement.studio and declared geist-font origin; renderer and docs/site Geist WOFF2 bytes compare equal.
OFL declarations require preserving applicable notice/license; neither CSS importing a font nor byte equality proves packaged notice inclusion or independently authenticates upstream origin.

Lucide imports and KaTeX CSS identify dependency-owned art/font boundaries. Manifest dependency declarations were located, but dependency package notices and final bundled font closure were not read/installed. Native/runtime/plugin dependency notices remain RP-A1 packaging ownership.
futureAcceptance: Verify the exact pinned Nerd/Geist/KaTeX/Lucide distribution licenses and binary origin, retain relevant copyright/reserved-name conditions, and inspect installed notices and offline glyph fallback without changing metrics.

contracts.title: Telemetry consent and persistent identity
sourceCharacterization: Consent precedence: DNT true/1 after trim/case fold, product disable true/1, nonempty CI markers, then persisted true enabled / false user opt-out / null or absent pending. Empty CI values do not disable, despite a broader source comment.

Unexpected disable values warn once per variable name and include the raw supplied value; never copy environment values into this artifact. Persistence helper accepts complete existing cohort state, preserves explicit partial opt-out/cohort data, defaults old-install missing consent to null and fresh-install missing consent to true, and creates UUID only if missing.

Stable install ID comes from settings, with a separate session UUID. This is pseudonymous identifying state, not proof of anonymity. Durable save/restart behavior is owned by settings integration; the migration helper alone does not prove a disk write.

Telemetry consent and diagnostic consent are different: observability checks environment, not stored telemetryOptIn. DNT/product disable stop bundle collection admission while allowing local logs; diagnostic disable/CI stop both. Initialized observability status caches that resolution.
futureAcceptance: In isolated environments assert true/false/null/missing and every env precedence, including empty CI, invalid-value logging without exposing a synthetic secret, fresh/old installs and restart persistence. Root decide intended correction to default opt-in/banner behavior explicitly.

contracts.title: Telemetry SDK lifecycle and admission caps
sourceCharacterization: Transport requires official compile flag plus stable/rc channel and nonempty injected write key. No runtime destination override is part of this client; original hard-coded destination and injected project key are reference-only and must be independently provisioned for Drogon.

SDK construction precedes disabled/pending opt-out handling, so source track gates do not prove SDK-constructor network silence. Config uses flushAt20, flushInterval10s, maxQueueSize5000, disableGeoip and no-person-profile capture property.

track gates official/channel, shutdown/client/store/common state, event burst admission, live consent, strict validation, then capture. Burst caps30/event/min,20/error/min and1000/session are consumed before consent/validation; IPC consent mutations share cap5/session. Store/capture throws are not universally swallowed.

Opt-in persists before SDK optIn and the event; old-install pending app_opened emits at most once. Opt-out captures its transition through a direct enqueue path, waits for matching SDK event+UUID or1s timeout, then optOut; enqueue is not server receipt. Banner dismissal persists true and suppresses opt-in event, though app_opened can emit.

Direct opt-out capture does not repeat DNT resolution; app_opened marks before track, so a dropped admission can consume the once guard. Shutdown gates future events before SDK shutdown(2000), catches rejection; actual SDK deadline/delivery behavior is external and unrun.
futureAcceptance: Use a pinned SDK fixture with synthetic configuration and a network spy to prove no requests when disabled/nonofficial/constructor-only, exercise cap boundaries and opt-in/out races, SDK enqueue failure/timeout, shutdown deadline, and independently provisioned destinations.

contracts.title: Telemetry validator, IPC provenance and field allowlists
sourceCharacterization: Common props strictly bound app/platform/arch/os/version and install/session IDs. Event schemas strictly reject unknown keys and raw error-message/stack fields where forbidden; registry was read only1–100, so this is shared admission characterization, not a new exhaustive per-event schema review.

Validator uses eventSchemas[name] rather than an own-property check: direct prototype names can reach a non-schema value and throw at safeParse. Normal track uses burst-cap own-property admission first; do not label the ordinary public capture path exploitable from this helper alone.

Validation warnings are deduplicated with bounded256-entry cache and60s pruning, but event names/issue paths can appear in logs. Main cohort classification replaces renderer values even with undefined.

Four IPC handlers reject nonstring names, main-owned event names, invalid property shape and nonboolean opt-in; null/undefined props normalize to{}. Arrays pass the first object-shaped admission and then face schema validation. Main-owned set denial has sample assertions rather than exhaustive six-name coverage.
Sender event is unused in these handlers. E3 owns enclosing IPC renderer admission; no sender authentication guarantee is inferred from these helper signatures.
futureAcceptance: Retain all existing schema/IPC assertions, add direct prototype-name helper cases and all six main-only names, unknown/nested fields, warning leakage/cap, cohort overwrite and unauthorized-sender integration.

contracts.title: Diagnostic preview, retained bytes, consent and local persistence
sourceCharacterization: Main retains generated bundle payload plus temp path by random bundle ID; renderer receives metadata only. Lookback finite values floor/clamp1..43200 minutes; otherwise collection default applies. Map TTL15min, max8 with pruning after insertion, unref timers and best-effort unlink. No startup orphan sweep is present in this module.

Preview directory mkdir0700 and write0600 are creation-mode requests; existing directory modes are not tightened here and there is no Windows ACL repair, exclusive/no-follow write or actual POSIX/ACL proof. Failure/crash may leave preview files.

Upload requires valid retained ID, prior successful shell.openPath and bundle-enabled status, then native Send/Cancel defaulting Cancel. It re-resolves the retained ID/status after confirmation before choosing endpoint and upload. shell.openPath success is not evidence the user read the file.

Upload sends original main-retained payload, so edits in an opened preview do not alter submitted bytes. Cancel/error retain state until TTL; success deletes state. There is no per-bundle inflight dedupe in this handler, so simultaneous confirmed uploads need a separate acceptance case.

Status recheck uses cached observability consent after initialization, not a fresh environment read or settings telemetryOptIn check. Delete validates ticket and endpoint but has no bundleEnabled gate, allowing cleanup independently of collection consent.
Desktop local profile owns retained bytes/preview and local trace/daemon-log collection. No SSH-host log fetch is implied.
futureAcceptance: Retain opened/cancelled/expired/discarded-while-dialog tests; add concurrent sends, cached-consent changes, no-follow/existing-directory/Windows ACL decisions and crash-orphan cleanup in disposable profiles. UI must accurately explain retained payload; root decide correction if editable preview is intended.

contracts.title: Feedback, images and crash-report formatting
contracts.owner: WP-ENG-OBS / E1 consent UI / service owner
sourceCharacterization: Public feedback forces feedback report type; anonymous mode nulls supplied login/email, not free-text or image metadata. Nonanonymous identity is forwarded without verification inside this helper despite a test title saying verified. Null/undefined whole args can throw; text/identity are not comprehensively schema/size checked in this public wrapper.

Images accept at most4, each nonempty Uint8Array<=8MiB, exact PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF MIME allowlist and generated filenames. Typed-array subviews preserve their exact bytes. There is no magic-byte validation, transcoding or EXIF scrub here; up to32MiB image content plus framing can be sent.

Images use multipart60s and no retry even5xx;2xx is transport success but imagesDelivered needs explicittrue or absent-field oktrue. NonJSON, oversized response>64KiB or body-read error leaves delivery unconfirmed; deadline abort is failure. Crash lane discards images including malformed ones.

Plain JSON uses10s and one retry on thrown/network or>=500. Diagnostic multipart uses60s and eligible report-only10s fallback for400/403/404/408/413/415/422/>=500/exceptions. Initial host is fixed, but Electron fetch redirect policy is not set: do not claim redirect destination enforcement.

Formatting caps raw notes at16000 before trim/sanitize, user notes at8000 including ellipsis, puts fenced/indented notes before machine data, and caps final text at64000 JavaScript characters, not bytes. Per-detail string sanitizer returns240 or4000 characters plus three-character suffix when truncated.

Crash store sanitizes newly recorded/attached detail values and breadcrumbs, but disk read only checks reports is an array and slices5; existing loaded records/top-level fields are not re-sanitized before formatting. The leaf statement safe because sanitized at write time is too broad.
futureAcceptance: Retain full feedback/image/shared-format assertions; add malformed args, spoofed identity, magic-byte/EXIF policy, multibyte endpoint limits, redirects, legacy/tampered stored values and synthetic secret classes. Root separate current behavior from intended privacy corrections.

contracts.title: Existing G9 transport and crash submission contracts
sourceCharacterization: Reuse root-accepted parity-diagnostic-tray-contracts G9 for crash-selection/deduplication, fallback ordering and diagnostic HTTP endpoints; no endpoint probe or repeated source census.

Crash path selects explicit report or uncaptured context, supports explicitly dismissed reports, guards concurrent selected report IDs, and records recent successes in process-local insertion-ordered256 set. Remote success stays successful when local markSent fails; no cross-restart/server idempotency proof.

Support lane tokens bind submission ID and declared bytes; client checks token/upload_url/max_bytes, does not validate expires_at. Upload URL allows http(s), rejects HTTPS downgrade, compares URL.host including port, not full origin. Bearer NDJSON upload requires nonempty ticket_id; delete validates ticket.

HTTP helper bounds response1MiB, accepts2xx JSON including empty{}, hides non2xx body, cleans listeners and returns generic network errors. Token/delete10s and upload30s are request timeouts, not established absolute whole-operation deadlines.
Existing accepted mock HTTP execution evidence is historical and scoped, not a new run or a live backend test. Crash log include-default and3-day lookback remain source behavior.
futureAcceptance: Re-run original bundle/upload HTTP/crash submission suites in a writable pinned baseline and port unchanged, then use isolated synthetic backend to assert downgrade/port/redirect/expiry/byte-cap/timeout/idempotency/fallback and persistence-after-success behavior.

contracts.title: Host scope and external service implementation boundary
sourceCharacterization: Runtime RPC exposes diagnostics.memory on that execution host; this is a memory snapshot, not the desktop support-bundle API. Web preload diagnostics return null or explicit unavailable errors; no SSH profile collection/upload proxy is characterized here.

Client bundle source explicitly says only the client ships and refers endpoint contract to telemetry-error-tracking.md. Bounded source searches in cloud and docs/site found no implementation of the feedback/token/upload/delete endpoints; this establishes an external source gap in the inspected trees, not absence from every repository.

Backend token authorization/expiry/one-use policy, server redaction, actual size enforcement, storage retention/access controls, delete/idempotency and downstream forwarding are unavailable here. Source comments asserting server ingest redaction are design declarations, not inspected server code.

Original telemetry/feedback/build endpoint strings are reference provenance only. Drogon requires independently provisioned projects, service destinations, keys and policy; this audit neither copies keys nor contacts those services.

The referenced telemetry-error-tracking.md was not found by the bounded tracked-file navigation query, and docs/telemetry-error-tracking.md does not exist at the inspected path. Treat that comment as an unavailable design pointer; accepted G9 client contracts remain the concrete source evidence.
futureAcceptance: Root obtain and pin authorized backend implementation or approve independent Drogon service contract. Then synthetic service tests must cover auth, expiry, caps, redaction, failure atomicity, retention/delete and no cross-host data collection.

contracts.title: Reviewed collector, redaction, storage and native capture integration
sourceCharacterization: Leaf OBS-COL-01..13 and13b are retained as14 local contract records across13 unique source files. Lead read the entire leaf report/JSON, recomputed every supplied blob identity, and independently read bundle, both redactors, sink, crash store, Crashpad capture, durable breadcrumb and shared formatter; tracer/instrumentation/breadcrumb coalescing remain leaf-source reviewed with explicit unread test pointers.

Collection processes trace family first, then daemon family, newest file/line first within each; it does not globally sort both families by timestamp. It accepts arbitrary JSON objects, skips arrays/primitives/malformed JSON, keeps missing/unparseable time, filters valid end-time/daemon ts by cutoff, and applies server-mode redaction.50MiB stat guard is subject to file growth between stat/read;4MiB cumulative output includes header, skips individually oversized records, then stops entire collection on aggregate overflow. Trusted metadata/header itself has no standalone truncation guard.

Trace sink defaults10MiB x10 files,32-record batch threshold,200ms flush. mkdir/open initialization can throw; chmod is best effort, writes retry once then drop; failed rotation/reopen and partial writes are not a universal never-throw or hard disk-cap guarantee. Rotation test named total cap actually asserts less than2x configured product, not <=product.

Span redaction deliberately preserves filesystem paths and span/event names; client-mode drops structured secret key families, server-mode additionally drops exact identity key forms. These controls do not prove every PII field or unrecognized secret removed. Local sink does not itself call redactor; tracer finalization and bundle collection are the read client sites. Server-ingest pass appears only as a source design declaration here.

Crash detail sanitizer is a separate primitive allowlist with path-value and named-key path redaction, secret regexes and bounded strings; no broad structured secret-key removal. Lead read complete shared crash/redactor assertion bodies: the span suite covers AWS secret assignment and bare JWT, while shared crash cases cover access-key ID and Bearer JWT rather than those two forms. Candidate privacy defect AO-REDACT-01 requires synthetic regression and root correction decision, not a live-secret demonstration.

Crash store uses serialized write-temp/rename and5-record cap, not byte-bound file reads, private mode setting, fsync durability or schema validation of disk data. Windows retry50/100/150/200/250ms and one best-effort ACL repair; underlying ACL implementation remains E5 native ownership, not proven by mocks.

Crashpad starts once with uploadToServer:false, ignoreSystemCrashHandler:false, compress:false; local raw dumps contain process memory and are not scrubbed text attachments. Poll8s/250ms reads candidates no older than max(crash-30s,start), size<=64MiB before read; parser expected process type and claimed/reserved sets gate selection. Native filesystem operations can exceed polling deadline; no absolute8s guarantee.

Prune targets128MiB/64files but ALWAYS preserves newest, reserved and claimed files; failed deletes are ignored. Therefore those budgets are best effort, not absolute hard caps. Raw dump access, native/OS crash-reporter behavior and parser correctness need platform tests; uploadToServer:false does not prove OS system reporter has no independently configured behavior.

Durable breadcrumb records lifecycle-tagged sanitized data, writes a crash.breadcrumb span and flushes the active sink. Coalesced suppressed repeats return before span/flush; leaf every write/failure language is narrowed to emitted records. Flush is not fsync/power-loss durability.
futureAcceptance: Retain all original57 diagnostic allocation suites and exact leaf partial/pointer associations; read unreviewed assertion bodies before porting. Run isolated synthetic disk-full/short-write/rotation/reopen, tampered-store, multibyte/redaction, native dump/ACL and coalescing cases without real profiles, raw memory or uploads.

leafCorrections.finding: Leaf blobSha256 fields and SHA256 column actually contain40-hex git blob SHA1 values. All14 match locally recomputed git-blob SHA1; lead companion supplies real64-hex whole-byte SHA256. These are current working-byte identities, not independently root-verified pinned blobs.
Leaf claims13 contracts; its JSON contains14 records including13b, across13 unique files. These counts are bookkeeping only.

Leaf F1 redaction asymmetry is supported by lead source and full shared/redactor test-body reads; no real or synthetic execution occurred.
